Script.name: explorer/svg
Script.script:
--[[ Explorer — SVG renderer Sean Stoves, 2026-07-31
Draws area maps in the Gaardian house style, because that's the style every Aardwolf player already reads fluently. Taken from maps.gaardian.com's own renderer rather than eyeballed:
plain white box, black border stroke 2 normal room green border stroke 5 area entrance red border stroke 2/4 aggressive mobs (we can't know) "PK" red bold 10px, bottom left pk room room NAME across the top, wrapped not a room number short bar across a link door
The important one is what Gaardian does NOT do: it never runs a line across the map for a distant exit. It draws a stub with a link marker and only shows the connector when you click it, because long diagonals turn a map into a cat's cradle. Same here - stub, grey dot, and the full line fades in on hover for anyone who opens the file in a browser.
Three departures, all deliberate:
* boxes are 140x56 rather than 100x60. Gaardian hand-edits names to fit; we don't, so the box has to hold a real one. * the room id sits under the name. Gaardian has no use for it, we do - it's what you actually type at the MUD. * Gaardian flattens an area onto one hand-placed grid. We have real z coordinates, so each level gets its own. Up/down stop being a fudged diagonal and become what they are.
Aggro and graffiti are hand-curated on Gaardian's side and aren't in mapper data, so they're left out rather than invented. The flags we do have - shop, bank, trainer, healer, guild, safe, maze - get corner letters and a legend. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.explorer = aardkit.explorer or {}
local EX = aardkit.explorer
local RW, RH = 140, 56 -- room box; Gaardian's 100 was too tight for -- one-line names once we stopped hand-editing them local GAPX, GAPY = 34, 26 -- space between boxes for the connectors local MARGIN = 30
local FLAGMARK = { shop = "$", bank = "B", trainer = "T", healer = "H", guild = "G", safe = "+", maze = "?", }
local FLAGNAME = { ["$"] = "shop", ["B"] = "bank", ["T"] = "trainer", ["H"] = "healer", ["G"] = "guild", ["+"] = "safe", ["?"] = "maze", }
local function esc(s) return (tostring(s or ""):gsub("&", "&"):gsub("<", "<"):gsub(">", ">") :gsub('"', """):gsub("'", "'")) end
-- Greedy wrap at roughly the width Tahoma 12px gives us. Gaardian drops to 10px -- once a name runs past 39 characters; same rule here. local function wrap(name, maxchars) local lines, cur = {}, "" for word in tostring(name or ""):gmatch("%S+") do if cur == "" then cur = word elseif #cur + 1 + #word <= maxchars then cur = cur .. " " .. word else lines[#lines + 1] = cur cur = word end if #lines >= 3 then break end end if cur ~= "" and #lines < 4 then lines[#lines + 1] = cur end return lines end
local function flags_of(info) local set = {} for f in tostring(info or ""):gmatch("[^,%s]+") do set[f:lower()] = true end return set end
--- -- one z-level -> one <g> ---
-- Rank the coordinates actually in use instead of drawing the raw span. Areas -- are full of holes - Aardington's ground floor spans 14 columns for 8 occupied -- ones - and rendering the holes is what made the old maps mostly whitespace. -- Gaardian gets compactness by hand-placing every room; collapsing unused rows -- and columns is the automated equivalent. Order is preserved, so the map still -- reads true; only the empty space goes. local function rank(rooms, key) local seen, vals = {}, {} for _, r in pairs(rooms) do if not seen[r[key]] then seen[r[key]] = true; vals[#vals + 1] = r[key] end end table.sort(vals) local idx = {} for i, v in ipairs(vals) do idx[v] = i - 1 end return idx, #vals end
local function draw_level(o, rooms, links, oy, label) local xi, nx = rank(rooms, "x") local yi, ny = rank(rooms, "y") if nx == 0 then return oy, 0, 0 end
-- SVG y grows downward, the MUD's y grows north, so flip it local function px(r) return MARGIN + xi[r.x] * (RW + GAPX) end local function py(r) return oy + (ny - 1 - yi[r.y]) * (RH + GAPY) end
local w = MARGIN * 2 + nx * (RW + GAPX) local h = ny * (RH + GAPY)
if label then o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<text x="%d" y="%d" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#333">%s</text>', MARGIN, oy - 8, esc(label)) end
-- connectors first so the boxes sit on top of the line ends for _, l in ipairs(links) do local a, b = rooms[l.from], rooms[l.to] if a and b then local x1, y1 = px(a) + RW / 2, py(a) + RH / 2 local x2, y2 = px(b) + RW / 2, py(b) + RH / 2 local far = math.abs(xi[a.x] - xi[b.x]) > 1 or math.abs(yi[a.y] - yi[b.y]) > 1
if not far and not l.special then o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<line x1="%.0f" y1="%.0f" x2="%.0f" y2="%.0f" stroke="#000" stroke-width="2"/>', x1, y1, x2, y2) if l.door then -- short bar across the link, the way a door reads on paper local mx, my = (x1 + x2) / 2, (y1 + y2) / 2 local dx, dy = x2 - x1, y2 - y1 local len = math.max(1, math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)) local nx, ny = -dy / len * 7, dx / len * 7 o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<line x1="%.0f" y1="%.0f" x2="%.0f" y2="%.0f" stroke="#000" stroke-width="3"/>', mx - nx, my - ny, mx + nx, my + ny) end else -- Gaardian never runs a line across the map for a distant exit. -- It draws a short stub with a link marker and only shows the -- full connector once you click it, because long diagonals turn -- a map into a cat's cradle. Same here: stub plus marker, and -- the whole line fades in on hover for anyone who opens the file -- in a browser. Static viewers just see the stubs. o[#o + 1] = '<g class="lk">' o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<line class="far" x1="%.0f" y1="%.0f" x2="%.0f" y2="%.0f" stroke="#f28c28" stroke-width="3"/>', x1, y1, x2, y2) local tip = esc(a.name .. " <-> " .. b.name .. (l.label and (" (" .. l.label .. ")") or "")) for _, e in ipairs({ { a, x1, y1, x2, y2 }, { b, x2, y2, x1, y1 } }) do local rr, sx, sy, tx, ty2 = e[1], e[2], e[3], e[4], e[5] local dx, dy = tx - sx, ty2 - sy local len = math.max(1, math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)) dx, dy = dx / len, dy / len -- start at the box edge, not the middle local ex = sx + dx * (math.abs(dx) > math.abs(dy) and RW / 2 or RH / 2) local ey = sy + dy * (math.abs(dx) > math.abs(dy) and RW / 2 or RH / 2) o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<line x1="%.0f" y1="%.0f" x2="%.0f" y2="%.0f" stroke="#000" stroke-width="2"/>', ex, ey, ex + dx * 14, ey + dy * 14) o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<circle cx="%.0f" cy="%.0f" r="5" fill="#bbb" stroke="#555" stroke-width="1">' .. '<title>%s</title></circle>', ex + dx * 20, ey + dy * 20, tip) end if l.label then o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<text x="%.0f" y="%.0f" font-size="9" fill="#8a4b00" text-anchor="middle">%s</text>', (x1 + x2) / 2, (y1 + y2) / 2 - 3, esc(l.label)) end o[#o + 1] = '</g>' end end end
for _, r in ipairs(EX.sorted(rooms)) do local x, y = px(r), py(r) local stroke, width = "#000", 2 if r.entrance then stroke, width = "#0a0", 5 end
o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<rect x="%d" y="%d" width="%d" height="%d" fill="#fff" stroke="%s" stroke-width="%d">' .. '<title>%s #%s%s</title></rect>', x, y, RW, RH, stroke, width, esc(r.name), r.id, r.info ~= "" and (" [" .. esc(r.info) .. "]") or "")
local fs = #tostring(r.name or "") >= 39 and 10 or 12 local lines = wrap(r.name, fs == 10 and 26 or 22) local ty = y + 16 for i, ln in ipairs(lines) do o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<text x="%.0f" y="%.0f" font-size="%d" fill="#000" text-anchor="middle">%s</text>', x + RW / 2, ty + (i - 1) * (fs + 2), fs, esc(ln)) end
o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<text x="%.0f" y="%.0f" font-size="9" fill="#777" text-anchor="middle">%s</text>', x + RW / 2, y + RH - 5, r.id)
local f = flags_of(r.info) if f.pk then o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<text x="%d" y="%d" font-size="10" font-weight="bold" fill="#d00">PK</text>', x + 4, y + RH - 4) end
local marks = {} for name, ch in pairs(FLAGMARK) do if f[name] then marks[#marks + 1] = ch end end table.sort(marks) if #marks > 0 then o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<text x="%d" y="%d" font-size="10" fill="#0057b8" text-anchor="end">%s</text>', x + RW - 4, y + RH - 4, esc(table.concat(marks, " "))) end
-- up/down are real levels now, so say where rather than drawing a fake -- diagonal into another grid if r.ud and r.ud ~= "" then o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<text x="%d" y="%d" font-size="10" fill="#555" text-anchor="end">%s</text>', x + RW - 4, y + 12, esc(r.ud)) end end
return oy + h + 40, w, h end
--- -- legend — only the flags this area actually uses ---
local function draw_legend(o, used, oy, w) local items = {} if used.entrance then items[#items + 1] = { "#0a0", "green box = area entrance" } end if used.pk then items[#items + 1] = { "#d00", "PK = player killing" } end if used.door then items[#items + 1] = { "#000", "bar across a link = door" } end if used.far then items[#items + 1] = { "#555", "grey dot = exit to a room elsewhere on the map (hover to trace it)" } end for ch in pairs(used.marks or {}) do items[#items + 1] = { "#0057b8", ch .. " = " .. (FLAGNAME[ch] or "?") } end if #items == 0 then return oy end
table.sort(items, function(a, b) return a[2] < b[2] end) o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<text x="%d" y="%d" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#333">Legend</text>', MARGIN, oy) local y = oy + 16 for _, it in ipairs(items) do o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<text x="%d" y="%d" font-size="11" fill="%s">%s</text>', MARGIN, y, it[1], esc(it[2])) y = y + 14 end return y + 10 end
--- -- entry point ---
-- levels: { [z] = { rooms = {id->room}, links = {..} } } function EX.build_svg(title, levels, subtitle) local o, oy = {}, MARGIN + 40 local maxw = 600 local used = { marks = {} }
local zs = {} for z in pairs(levels) do zs[#zs + 1] = z end table.sort(zs, function(a, b) return a > b end) -- highest level first
local body = {} for _, z in ipairs(zs) do local lv = levels[z] for _, r in pairs(lv.rooms) do if r.entrance then used.entrance = true end local f = flags_of(r.info) if f.pk then used.pk = true end for name, ch in pairs(FLAGMARK) do if f[name] then used.marks[ch] = true end end end for _, l in ipairs(lv.links) do if l.door then used.door = true end local a, b = lv.rooms[l.from], lv.rooms[l.to] if l.special or (a and b and (math.abs(a.x - b.x) > 1 or math.abs(a.y - b.y) > 1)) then used.far = true end end local label = #zs > 1 and ("Level " .. z) or nil local ny, w = draw_level(body, lv.rooms, lv.links, oy, label) oy, maxw = ny, math.max(maxw, w) end
oy = draw_legend(body, used, oy, maxw)
o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="%d" height="%d" viewBox="0 0 %d %d" ' .. 'font-family="Tahoma,Verdana,sans-serif">', maxw, oy, maxw, oy) o[#o + 1] = '<style>.far{opacity:0}.lk:hover .far{opacity:1}' .. '.lk:hover circle{fill:#f28c28}</style>' o[#o + 1] = string.format('<rect width="%d" height="%d" fill="#fff"/>', maxw, oy) o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<text x="%d" y="%d" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#000">%s</text>', MARGIN, MARGIN, esc(title)) if subtitle then o[#o + 1] = string.format( '<text x="%d" y="%d" font-size="11" fill="#666">%s</text>', MARGIN, MARGIN + 16, esc(subtitle)) end for _, s in ipairs(body) do o[#o + 1] = s end o[#o + 1] = '</svg>' return table.concat(o, "\n") end
-- stable draw order so a re-export diffs cleanly in git function EX.sorted(rooms) local out = {} for _, r in pairs(rooms) do out[#out + 1] = r end table.sort(out, function(a, b) return a.id < b.id end) return out end

Script.name: explorer
Script.script:
--[[ Explorer — area maps from Mudlet's own map Sean Stoves, 2026-07-31
The MUSHclient version read the mapper's SQLite file and *inferred* room positions by walking the exit graph, nudging boxes sideways whenever two landed on the same square. It also treated up/down as a diagonal step, which quietly folded every floor of a tower onto one plane. That's why its output never looked like a real map.
Mudlet stores real coordinates, so none of that guessing is needed: getRoomCoordinates gives x, y and z outright. Rooms go where they actually are, and each z becomes its own grid instead of a fudge.
Read-only. It never moves you and never touches the map. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.explorer = aardkit.explorer or {}
local EX = aardkit.explorer local U = aardkit.util
local CFG = U.load("explorer", { dir = "maps" })
local panel = aardkit.panel.new({ name = "explorer", title = "Explorer", x = "10px", y = "300px", width = 380, height = 260, })
EX.panel = panel
local DIRDELTA = { north = { 0, 1 }, south = { 0, -1 }, east = { 1, 0 }, west = { -1, 0 }, northeast = { 1, 1 }, northwest = { -1, 1 }, southeast = { 1, -1 }, southwest = { -1, -1 }, }
local function outdir(d) return d == "up" or d == "down" end
--- -- map access ---
local function areas() local t = getAreaTable and getAreaTable() or {} local out = {} for name, id in pairs(t) do out[#out + 1] = { name = name, id = id } end table.sort(out, function(a, b) return a.name:lower() < b.name:lower() end) return out end
-- partial match, current area when nothing's given function EX.resolve(want) want = U.trim(want or "") if want == "" then local here = getPlayerRoom and getPlayerRoom() local aid = here and getRoomArea and getRoomArea(here) if not aid then return nil, "Can't tell what area you're in." end for _, a in ipairs(areas()) do if a.id == aid then return a end end return nil, "Area " .. tostring(aid) .. " isn't in the area table." end local lw = want:lower() local hits = {} for _, a in ipairs(areas()) do if a.name:lower() == lw then return a end if a.name:lower():find(lw, 1, true) then hits[#hits + 1] = a end end if #hits == 1 then return hits[1] end if #hits == 0 then return nil, "No area matching '" .. want .. "'." end local names = {} for _, a in ipairs(hits) do names[#names + 1] = a.name end return nil, #hits .. " areas match: " .. table.concat(names, ", ") end
-- everything the renderer needs, grouped by z function EX.collect(areaid) local ids = getAreaRooms and getAreaRooms(areaid) or {} local mine, levels = {}, {} local n = 0
for _, id in pairs(ids) do local x, y, z = getRoomCoordinates(id) if x then mine[id] = { x = x, y = y, z = z or 0 } n = n + 1 end end if n == 0 then return nil, 0 end
for id, p in pairs(mine) do local z = p.z levels[z] = levels[z] or { rooms = {}, links = {} }
local info = "" if getRoomUserData then info = getRoomUserData(id, "info") or "" end
local ud = {} local entrance = false local exits = getRoomExits and getRoomExits(id) or {}
for dir, dest in pairs(exits) do if outdir(dir) then -- real level change; note it rather than drawing a fake diagonal ud[#ud + 1] = (dir == "up") and "↑" or "↓" end -- an exit leaving the area is where you come in from if not mine[dest] then entrance = true end end table.sort(ud)
levels[z].rooms[id] = { id = id, x = p.x, y = p.y, info = info, name = (getRoomName and getRoomName(id)) or ("#" .. id), entrance = entrance, ud = table.concat(ud, ""), } end
-- links, deduped, only between rooms on the same level for id, p in pairs(mine) do local lv = levels[p.z] local doors = getDoors and getDoors(id) or {} for dir, dest in pairs(getRoomExits and getRoomExits(id) or {}) do local q = mine[dest] if q and q.z == p.z and id < dest and DIRDELTA[dir] then lv.links[#lv.links + 1] = { from = id, to = dest, door = (doors[dir] or 0) > 0 or nil, } end end -- special exits are the followable oddities; label them local ok, sp = pcall(getSpecialExits, id) if ok and type(sp) == "table" then for dest, cmd in pairs(sp) do local d = tonumber(dest) if type(cmd) == "table" then cmd = next(cmd) end if d and mine[d] and mine[d].z == p.z then lv.links[#lv.links + 1] = { from = math.min(id, d), to = math.max(id, d), special = true, label = tostring(cmd), } end end end end
return levels, n end
--- -- output ---
local function outdir_path() local d = getMudletHomeDir() .. "/" .. (CFG.dir or "maps") pcall(lfs.mkdir, d) return d end
local function safe(s) return (tostring(s or "area"):gsub("[^%w%-]+", "_"):gsub("^_+", ""):gsub("_+$", "")) end
local function write(path, body) local fh, err = io.open(path, "w") if not fh then return nil, tostring(err) end fh:write(body) fh:close() return true end
function EX.svg(want) local a, err = EX.resolve(want) if not a then U.warn(err); return end
local levels, n = EX.collect(a.id) if not levels then U.warn("'" .. a.name .. "' has no rooms with coordinates.") return end
local nz = 0 for _ in pairs(levels) do nz = nz + 1 end local sub = n .. " rooms" .. (nz > 1 and (", " .. nz .. " levels") or "")
local body = EX.build_svg(a.name, levels, sub) local path = outdir_path() .. "/map_" .. safe(a.name) .. ".svg" local ok, werr = write(path, body) if not ok then U.err("Couldn't write " .. path .. ": " .. werr); return end
U.ok("Wrote " .. path .. " (" .. sub .. ")") EX.paint(a.name .. " -> " .. sub) end
function EX.json(want) local a, err = EX.resolve(want) if not a then U.warn(err); return end
local levels, n = EX.collect(a.id) if not levels then U.warn("'" .. a.name .. "' has no rooms with coordinates."); return end
local dump = { area = a.name, id = a.id, rooms = {}, links = {} } for z, lv in pairs(levels) do for _, r in pairs(lv.rooms) do dump.rooms[#dump.rooms + 1] = { id = r.id, name = r.name, x = r.x, y = r.y, z = z, info = r.info, } end for _, l in ipairs(lv.links) do dump.links[#dump.links + 1] = { from = l.from, to = l.to, door = l.door and true or nil, special = l.special and true or nil, cmd = l.label, } end end
local path = outdir_path() .. "/map_" .. safe(a.name) .. ".json" local ok, werr = write(path, yajl.to_string(dump)) if not ok then U.err("Couldn't write " .. path .. ": " .. werr); return end U.ok("Wrote " .. path .. " (" .. n .. " rooms)") end
function EX.all() local list = areas() U.note("Exporting " .. #list .. " areas - this writes a lot of files.") local done, empty = 0, 0 for _, a in ipairs(list) do local levels, n = EX.collect(a.id) if levels then local nz = 0 for _ in pairs(levels) do nz = nz + 1 end local body = EX.build_svg(a.name, levels, n .. " rooms" .. (nz > 1 and (", " .. nz .. " levels") or "")) if write(outdir_path() .. "/map_" .. safe(a.name) .. ".svg", body) then done = done + 1 end else empty = empty + 1 end end U.ok("Wrote " .. done .. " maps to " .. outdir_path() .. (empty > 0 and (" (" .. empty .. " areas had no coordinates)") or "")) end
--- -- panel ---
function EX.paint(last) if not panel.console then return end panel:clear() local list = areas() panel:cecho("<#e94560>Explorer<r>\n") panel:cecho("<#8a93a8>" .. #list .. " areas in the map<r>\n\n") local a = EX.resolve("") if a then local _, n = EX.collect(a.id) panel:cecho("<#c8d0dc>Here: <#3ad07a>" .. a.name .. "<r> <#8a93a8>(" .. (n or 0) .. " rooms)<r>\n") end panel:cecho("<#8a93a8>Out: " .. outdir_path() .. "<r>\n") if last then panel:cecho("\n<#c8d0dc>" .. last .. "<r>\n") end end
--- -- commands ---
function EX.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg)
if verb == "" then EX.paint() panel:toggle()
elseif verb == "svg" or verb == "map" then EX.svg(rest)
elseif verb == "json" then EX.json(rest)
elseif verb == "area" then EX.svg(rest)
elseif verb == "all" then EX.all()
elseif verb == "list" then local filter = U.trim(rest):lower() local rows, shown = {}, 0 for _, a in ipairs(areas()) do if filter == "" or a.name:lower():find(filter, 1, true) then local ids = getAreaRooms and getAreaRooms(a.id) or {} local n = 0 for _ in pairs(ids) do n = n + 1 end rows[#rows + 1] = { a.name, n .. " rooms" } shown = shown + 1 end end if shown == 0 then U.note("No areas match '" .. filter .. "'.") else U.help("Areas", rows) end
elseif verb == "dir" then local d = U.trim(rest) if d == "" then U.note("Maps go to " .. outdir_path()) else CFG.dir = d; U.save("explorer", CFG) U.ok("Maps now go to " .. outdir_path()) end
elseif verb == "dock" or verb == "embed" or verb == "hide" or verb == "show" then aardkit.panel.cmd("explorer " .. verb)
else U.help("explore", { { "explore", "show/hide the panel" }, { "explore svg [area]", "Gaardian-style SVG map (default: where you are)" }, { "explore json [area]", "rooms and links as JSON" }, { "explore all", "every area (writes a lot of files)" }, { "explore list [f]", "areas in the map, with room counts" }, { "explore dir [path]", "where maps get written" }, { "explore dock|embed|hide", "" }, { "" }, { "Reads Mudlet's map only - it never moves you or changes it." }, { "Each z level gets its own grid, so towers stay towers." }, }) end end
aardkit.register("explore", "area maps from the mapper, Gaardian style", EX.cmd)
